faq.a: No — and that is the whole point. Exam preparation teaches a student to pass a paper. NET teaches a student to speak, and then the paper is an easier problem. If the goal is IELTS we build a band plan; if the goal is a boardroom we build a speaking plan. Both start with the same diagnostic.

faq.q: My child has studied English for years and still won't speak. Why?
faq.a: Because the method trained that. A grammar-first classroom installs a translation step — listen, translate to Vietnamese, translate back, speak — and under pressure the third step never finishes. The student freezes, and then learns to stay quiet. That is not a broken child; it is a working machine doing what it was built to do. NET removes the translation step by never installing it: mostly-understood input, then output under zero judgment.

The brain acquires language fastest when it naturally understands about 60% of what it hears. Below that, the listener switches from understanding to decoding and learns nothing. So we choose material that is mostly comprehensible and let the new 40% arrive carried by the part the student already owns. No dictionary hunting mid-sentence.

faq.q: What is the 45/15 protocol, and why one hour?
faq.a: 45 minutes of passive input — a podcast, a YouTube video, real listening that fits into a commute or a gym session — and 15 minutes of high-intensity output: shadowing, mimicry, speaking out loud under a little pressure. One hour a day, fitted into the life the student already has. We do not add time to your week; we use the time that is already in it. Homework, as the classic form, is dead.

A pocket accountability engine, not a chatbot. Human memory deletes most unreinforced material within 48 hours. The AI-PET logs the exact points a student keeps struggling with and re-introduces them at 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days, and it tracks the 45/15 ratio daily. Miss a day and the streak decays. Tough Love Mode is the point: it refuses to let a student slide quietly back into Mouse Mode.

The doctrine's ladder, read from behaviour rather than grammar. Mouse (0–40): hesitation, whispering, apologising, the imposter voice. Cub (41–79): willing, but still waiting for permission. Tiger (80–100): immediate response, real volume, ownership of the room. A student's mode is read from what they do in the room, and the work is to move them up it.

faq.q: Do you really teach from age 1 to 70?
faq.a: Yes. Early-years sessions are play and ear-training; secondary sessions are the school's own Close-up and Global Success content, taught for output as well as for the test; adult sessions run from first sentences to boardroom negotiation. The method changes with the age; the direction does not.

The ones the schools actually teach from: Look and Global Success for primary English, Cambridge Primary Science, and Close-up A1+ through New Close Up B1+ for secondary, plus Science in English. Private sessions follow the school's pacing guide so the hour reinforces the week instead of competing with it.

At your home within the home zone — Lakeview City, District 2 and the surrounding districts — or online when that suits better. Business and corporate sessions can run at your office. The free 30-minute diagnostic is in-home if you are in the zone.

600,000 VND per hour for one-to-one tuition, in-home. That is the published rate. Blocks, group and corporate work are quoted by the coach after the diagnostic — this site deliberately does not invent a discount ladder, because a price on a website you then have to argue about is a worse experience than a price in a conversation.

The 100% Confidence Guarantee: we do not promise perfect grammar in 30 days. We promise that a student who follows the 45/15 protocol will completely lose the fear of opening their mouth to speak English. Take the first month. If there is no massive, measurable surge in speaking velocity and confidence, the tuition is refunded in full. The student risks nothing. It is quoted from the doctrine as written.

faq.q: What happens on the free diagnostic?
faq.a: Thirty minutes, in your home or online. A real conversation to find the level rather than a paper test, a reading of which of the three failures is in play (the translate-in-head delay, the fear, or the apology reflex), and one immediate win the student walks away with that same day. Then, if it is a fit, a timetable. If it is not, the coach says so.

faq.q: Can I take a placement test right now?
faq.a: Yes — the placement test on this site runs in your browser in about eight minutes, adapts to your answers, and gives you a CEFR level, a skill breakdown and a 45/15 plan without you creating an account or giving an email address. It is a real measurement and it says what it cannot measure.

faq.q: What about my data — do I have to sign up?
faq.a: No account, no app, no mailing list. Anything you type into this site is stored on your own device, and nothing leaves it until you choose a channel — WhatsApp, email, SMS, the share sheet or a file download — and press send yourself. The pages say this plainly because it is true.
Yes, and it is the same hour: 1-on-1, live, with the camera on. Online is how students outside the home zone and students who travel are taught. The 45/15 runs the same either way.

If you teach English in Ho Chi Minh City and want to work with the protocol rather than against it, the Teach for NET page sends your details straight to the lead trainer.
